title: How to Seal a Driveway: 7 DIY Steps for a Coat That Won't Peel
keywords: how to seal coat a driveway
best way to apply driveway sealer
what do i need to seal my driveway
how to apply driveway sealer properly
description: Seal a driveway in 2 days: clean and fill cracks on day one, squeegee 2 thin coats at 50°F+ on day two, then keep cars off 24-48 hours. Asphalt steps inside.
dek: Seal a driveway in 2 days: clean and fill cracks on day one, squeegee 2 thin coats at 50°F+ on day two, then keep cars off 24-48 hours.
intro: To seal a driveway, spend day one trimming, cleaning and filling cracks, then on day two squeegee two thin coats of sealer onto the dry asphalt when it is 50°F and rising, and keep cars off for 24 to 48 hours. That is the whole job for a typical two-car blacktop driveway of 600 to 900 square feet.

The coating itself is the easy part. Nearly every DIY seal job that flakes off within a year failed on prep: dust left in the texture, cracks left open, a damp shady strip, or a forecast nobody checked. This guide walks through each step in order, with the quantities and wait times printed on typical asphalt sealer labels, so your first coat holds up as well as a contractor's.
quickAnswer: Check that the driveway needs it (water soaks in, surface has gone gray), buy enough sealer for two coats plus one spare pail, then clean, degrease and let the asphalt dry for a full day. Fill every crack wider than 1/8 inch, cut in the edges with a brush, and pull two thin coats with a squeegee, the second at a right angle to the first. Walk on it after it is dry to the touch; drive on it after 24 to 48 hours.

blocks.p: Sealing an asphalt driveway is a two-day project for one person, or a long single day for two people who start early. Most of the effort goes into getting the surface clean and dry, because sealer only bonds to clean asphalt. The coating step takes a few hours per coat on a typical driveway.

Pick your weekend by the forecast, not the calendar. You want three days in a row that stay dry and above 50°F, day and night, so you have room for prep, both coats and the first night of curing. If the hourly forecast shows rain within 24 hours of the second coat, wait for the next window. This page covers asphalt; concrete needs a different product and method, covered in [how to seal a concrete driveway](/how-to-seal-a-concrete-driveway/).

sections.h: Does Your Driveway Actually Need Sealing?

blocks.p: Spend ten minutes looking before you spend money on pails. Sealing a driveway that does not need it wastes a weekend and, done too often, builds up a brittle crust that cracks on its own.

Pour a cup of water on three or four spots, including the tire paths. If it beads or sits in a puddle for a few minutes, the last coat is still working and you can wait. If the water darkens the asphalt and vanishes within a minute, the surface is absorbing, and in a cold climate that water freezes inside the pavement every winter night. That is the signal to seal.

Fresh blacktop is deep black because the binder on top is rich in oils. Sun oxidizes it to charcoal and then to a dusty gray, and the small stones start to stand proud of the surface. When most of the driveway is gray with exposed aggregate, it is due.

blocks.h3: Rule out the jobs sealer cannot do

blocks.p: A driveway paved in the last six to twelve months is too new; see [when to seal a new asphalt driveway](/when-should-you-seal-a-new-asphalt-driveway/). At the other end, alligator cracking, potholes and sunken sections are base failures. Sealer coats the top a few sheets of paper thick and will not hold failing pavement together. Get those patched or resurfaced first, and if you are still deciding whether to seal at all, the trade-offs are in [should asphalt driveways be sealed](/sealing-asphalt-driveway-pros-and-cons/).

sections.h: What Do You Need to Seal a Driveway?

blocks.p: You do not need specialist equipment for a residential driveway. A squeegee, a brush, a broom and a drill are the core tools; the rest is sealer, filler and protective gear.

Closes cracks up to about 1/2 inch

blocks.p: Multiply length by width for the driveway, then add any parking pad or turnaround. A 20 by 40 foot two-car driveway is 800 square feet. Most retail asphalt emulsion pails list roughly 250 to 400 square feet per 5-gallon pail per coat, and an old, rough, gray surface drinks from the low end of that range. Two coats at 300 square feet per pail on 800 square feet comes to about six pails. Buy a seventh and keep the receipt: running dry halfway down the driveway leaves a lap mark where the new batch meets coat that has already started to set.

Water-based asphalt emulsion and acrylic or polymer-modified sealers are the normal DIY choices. They clean up with water and are legal everywhere. Refined coal tar resists gasoline and oil better, but several states and many cities ban or restrict it over polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) concerns. Ranked options are in the [best asphalt driveway sealer](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) list, and the chemistry trade-offs are in [oil-based vs water-based driveway sealer](/oil-based-vs-water-based-driveway-sealer/).

sections.h: How Do You Clean a Driveway Before Sealing?

blocks.p: Clean asphalt is the difference between a coat that lasts three years and one that flakes in three months. Sealer grabs whatever is on top, so if that is pollen, sand or a film of dust, the coat bonds to the dirt instead of the pavement.

Run a string trimmer or edger along both sides so the full width of asphalt is exposed; grass hanging over the edge leaves an uncoated strip. Pull weeds out of cracks with their roots, or they will push through the filler within weeks. Sweep with a stiff push broom, then go over the whole surface with a leaf blower to lift the fine dust the broom leaves in the texture.

A garden hose with a jet nozzle and a scrub brush is enough for a driveway in decent shape. A pressure washer is faster on a dirty one, but use a wide fan tip and keep it moving; a narrow tip can tear binder and loosen stones on older asphalt. The [best surface cleaner for a pressure washer](/best-surface-cleaner-for-pressure-washer/) gives an even, streak-free clean on large driveways.

Scrub drip stains with a driveway degreaser and rinse well. Once dry, paint each remaining stain with oil spot primer so water-based sealer can bond over it instead of beading and peeling. Spots that are soft or gummy from a long leak need cutting out and patching. For stubborn stains, see [how to remove oil stains from a driveway](/how-to-remove-oil-stains-from-driveway/).

Give the washed driveway at least 24 hours of dry weather, and longer for shaded or low areas. Press a paper towel into the darkest-looking spots; if it comes up damp, wait. Sealer over trapped moisture is the most common cause of first-year peeling. Use the drying time to tape off door trim and walkway edges, lay cardboard on the garage apron, and park the cars on the street.

sections.h: How Do You Fill Cracks Before Sealing?

blocks.p: Cracks are where water gets under the pavement, so filling them protects the driveway more than the coating does. Do it on day one so the filler has time to set before sealer goes over it.

blocks.h3: Match the repair to the crack width

head: Crack or damage
Repair
rows: Sealer alone can bridge it, especially sand-filled products
Pourable rubberized filler or caulk-tube filler
Foam backer rod first, then filler on top

blocks.p: Blow or vacuum each crack clean and make sure it is dry. Fill slightly below the surface rather than mounding it, then smooth with a putty knife or the squeegee side of your tool so the patch does not stand up as a ridge under the coat.

Dig loose material out of potholes, fill with cold patch no more than about two inches at a time, and compact each layer hard with a hand tamper or by driving over a board laid on top. Overfill slightly so it finishes flush. Cold patch is a stopgap compared with hot mix, but it is adequate for small residential holes.

Check the filler label. Many water-based fillers want several hours to a full day before sealing. If the filler has shrunk into the crack overnight, top it up and let it set before you coat. Product picks by crack width are in the [best driveway crack filler](/best-driveway-crack-filler/) guide.

sections.h: How Do You Apply Driveway Sealer?

blocks.p: Start mid-morning on day two, once the dew has burned off and the asphalt is dry everywhere, including the shady side. Most asphalt sealer labels call for air and surface temperatures of at least 50°F and rising, with no rain for 24 hours or more afterward. The full temperature rules are in [minimum temperature for sealing a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/).

Sand and solids sink to the bottom during storage. A pail stirred only at the top spreads thin for the first half and lumpy for the second. Run a mixing paddle on a drill for two to three minutes, and restir when the pail is half empty because solids keep settling while you work.
Brush a strip four to six inches wide along the garage apron, walkways, landscape edging and the street. That way the squeegee never has to work close to surfaces you do not want coated.

blocks.h3: Pull it thin with a squeegee

blocks.p: Work from the top of the driveway toward the street so you never walk back across wet sealer. Pour a ribbon across the width, about three to four feet ahead of you, and pull it with the squeegee in long, overlapping passes. Finish each section in one direction so the texture lines up. You want a thin film you can still see the surface texture through. Push puddles out of low spots onto the next section.

If you stop for a break, end on a straight line across the driveway rather than in a ragged patch, and overlap only slightly when you restart. Thick ridges at overlaps dry slowly and look darker. On a very hot, sunny day, a light mist of water just ahead of the squeegee slows flash drying, but never leave standing water.

sections.h: How Many Coats of Driveway Sealer Do You Need?

blocks.p: Two thin coats is the standard on most asphalt sealer labels. The first soaks into the open texture of a weathered surface; the second evens out the color and builds the protective film.

blocks.h3: When to put on the second coat

blocks.p: Wait until the first coat is dry enough to walk on without leaving prints. On a warm, sunny day that is often four to eight hours. Cool or humid weather stretches it, so go by the surface, not the clock. Pull the second coat at a right angle to the first. Crossing directions fills in thin streaks and gives a uniform color. If the second coat would run into the evening as temperatures fall, do it the next morning instead.

A thin film releases its water evenly and bonds through its full depth. A thick coat skins on top while the layer underneath stays soft, which leads to tire marks, scuffing and in the worst cases sheets that peel off. Two coats at the label coverage rate use the same material as one heavy coat and end up harder and more even.

A driveway sealed two or three years ago that is still in fair shape can sometimes take a single maintenance coat, or just a touch-up in the tire paths. A first-time seal or a badly weathered surface needs both.

sections.h: How Long Before You Can Drive on a Sealed Driveway?

blocks.p: Most labels call for 24 to 48 hours before cars, and longer in cool or humid weather. Foot traffic is usually fine once the coat is dry to the touch and evenly black, often four to eight hours on a warm day.

Put sawhorses, trash cans or caution tape across the street end, and tell everyone in the house which door to use. Turn off sprinklers that reach the driveway for a day before and after, since irrigation does the same damage as a shower.

blocks.h3: Drive gently for the first week

blocks.p: The surface can feel firm under a shoe while the bottom of the film is still soft. Hot tires turning in place scrub soft sealer and leave marks that last until the next reseal. For the first week, roll straight in and out and avoid turning the wheel while the car is stopped.

Rain in the first few hours can wash uncured sealer off or leave spots. The fixes, from doing nothing to recoating, are in [rain after driveway sealing](/rain-after-driveway-sealing/). For each drying stage by sealer type, see [how long driveway sealer takes to dry](/how-long-for-driveway-sealer-to-dry/).

sections.h: How Do You Clean Up and Fix Problem Spots?

blocks.p: Clean tools before you take a break. Water-based sealer rinses off while wet and becomes very hard to remove once it dries on a squeegee or paddle. Rinse into a bucket or onto gravel, not into a storm drain.

Pull painter's tape while the edge is still slightly soft for a clean line; wait until it hardens and the tape can lift sealer with it. Wipe drips off concrete or brick with a damp rag right away. Dried splatter usually comes off with an asphalt remover or citrus cleaner and a stiff brush.

Thin spots show as lighter patches and can be brushed over once the main coats are dry. Lap marks and tire scuffs usually soften after a few weeks of sun. Peeling in one area almost always traces back to a dusty, damp or oily surface under that spot: scrape the loose material, clean, prime if needed and recoat that section.
A sealed, partly used pail keeps for touch-ups if it does not freeze. Let empty pails dry out completely before they go in the trash, and check local rules for disposing of liquid sealer.

sections.h: Is It Easy to Seal a Driveway Yourself?

blocks.p: Yes, for most homeowners. Sealing asphalt takes no special skill, just patience with prep and a good weather window. A first-timer working carefully can match a contractor's finish on a standard residential driveway.

A two-car driveway in fair shape with a handful of cracks is a comfortable weekend job. Materials for that size typically cost a fraction of a contractor quote; the [cost to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/) guide has the typical DIY and professional ranges side by side.

Hire a sealcoating crew for very long or steep driveways, heavy cracking that needs hot-pour crack sealant, or a schedule with no free weekend. Ask for a written quote that names the product, the number of coats, whether crack filling is included, and what happens if rain hits within a few hours.

blocks.h3: How often you will repeat it

blocks.p: Once sealed, most asphalt driveways need another coat every two to three years, not every spring. Sealing more often stacks up layers that crack and flake. The water test tells you when; the details are in [how often should you seal your driveway](/how-often-should-you-seal-your-driveway/), and the [best time to seal a driveway](/best-time-to-seal-driveway/) guide helps you pick the season.

mistakes: A quick sweep leaves fine sand and dust in the texture, and sealer bonds to that layer instead of the asphalt. It looks fine for a month and then peels in flakes. Sweep, blow, wash and let it dry fully. The extra hour of cleaning is the cheapest insurance on the job.

Finishing in one heavy pass is tempting, but a thick film skins on top and stays soft underneath, so it scuffs under tires and can peel in sheets. Two thin coats at the label coverage rate dry evenly, bond better and give a more uniform color for the same amount of sealer.

Sealer bridges hairlines, but anything wider than about 1/8 inch opens back up after the first winter and lets water under the pavement. Fill every crack with a proper filler and let it set before you coat, or the sealer protects the part of the driveway that needed it least.

Clear skies at breakfast say nothing about a 4 p.m. thunderstorm. Read the hourly forecast for the whole day and the following night, and confirm the overnight low stays above the label minimum. If the window is marginal, wait a week; a pail in the garage keeps, sealer in the gutter does not.
Driving on it the next morning

The surface can look dry and still be soft underneath, especially after a cool night. Tires leave marks that stay visible until the next reseal. Give it the full label time, usually 24 to 48 hours, add a day in cool or humid weather, and check the shady side with a fingernail first.
bottomLine: How well a driveway seal holds up depends on prep and weather far more than on the pail you buy. Clean it thoroughly, fill every crack wider than a pencil line, wait for a fully dry surface and a three-day dry forecast above 50°F, and lay down two thin coats instead of one thick one. Keep cars off for 24 to 48 hours and drive gently for a week. Do that and you will match a contractor's result for a fraction of the cost, then repeat the job every two to three years rather than every spring.

faqs.q: How long does it take to seal a driveway yourself?
faqs.a: Most of two days for a typical 600 to 900 square foot driveway. Day one goes to trimming, cleaning, degreasing and filling cracks. Day two covers both coats, a few hours each including the wait between them. Then allow 24 to 48 hours before driving on it, longer in cool or humid weather.

faqs.q: What do I need to seal my driveway?
faqs.a: You need enough asphalt sealer for two coats plus a spare pail, crack filler, oil spot primer, a squeegee and brush tool, an edging brush, a drill with a mixing paddle, a stiff broom, a leaf blower, a hose, painter's tape, gloves and old shoes. A pressure washer helps but is optional.

faqs.q: What is the best way to apply driveway sealer?
faqs.a: A squeegee is the best tool for most driveways. It spreads sealer quickly in a thin, even film and pushes it into the texture. Use a brush to cut in the edges and on very rough spots. Work from the garage toward the street, keep a wet edge, and pull the second coat at a right angle to the first.

faqs.q: Do I need to pressure wash my driveway before sealing?
faqs.a: No, but it helps on a dirty driveway. A hose with a jet nozzle, a stiff brush and a degreaser for oil spots cleans most driveways well enough. If you use a pressure washer, choose a wide fan tip and keep it moving so it does not strip binder from older asphalt. Either way, let it dry fully.

faqs.q: How many coats of driveway sealer should I apply?
faqs.a: Two thin coats is what most asphalt sealer labels recommend. The first soaks into the texture and the second evens the color and builds the film. A driveway sealed recently and still in fair condition can sometimes get by with one maintenance coat, but a first-time or neglected driveway needs two.

faqs.q: Can I seal my driveway in the fall?
faqs.a: Yes, if temperatures stay above the label minimum, usually 50°F, during application and for the next day or two. Early fall is often a good window because days are dry and mild. Late fall is riskier because cold nights and heavy dew slow curing, and a coat that does not cure before frost can fail by spring.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to seal a driveway yourself?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Materials for a typical driveway cost a fraction of what sealcoating contractors commonly quote for the same area. The trade-off is a weekend of work. For very large, steep or badly cracked driveways, a crew with spray equipment and hot-pour crack sealant can be worth the extra cost.
